items.q: Does GoHighLevel have a built-in AI receptionist?
items.a:
Yes. GoHighLevel's Voice AI agents can answer a business's calls on any GoHighLevel plan with no separate AI subscription: without an AI Employee plan, each call is billed from the prepaid wallet at $0.045 a minute for HighLevel's Voice Engine, plus the chosen voice, the model's tokens and the phone charges. HighLevel's help center lists what the agent can do during a call: transfer the caller to a human phone number, book an appointment on a HighLevel calendar, save details to contact fields, start a workflow and send a text.

Each agent is deployed on an LC Phone or Twilio number, either answering every call or acting as a backup when nobody picks up, around the clock or on a custom schedule. The receptionist does not come ready-made, though: someone has to write its instructions, set up the booking calendar and test it before real callers reach it.

items.q: Can an AI receptionist book appointments into my calendar?
items.a:
Most can, though not always on the cheapest plan. Rosie books straight into Google Calendar, Calendly, Acuity or Appointlet only from its $149 Scale plan; on the $49 Professional plan it texts callers a booking link instead. My AI Front Desk's pricing page says its AI handles booking, rescheduling and no-show follow-ups, and its one self-serve plan costs $99 a month. GoHighLevel's Voice AI books into HighLevel's own booking calendars, and HighLevel's help article asks for at least one to be configured with availability, appointment length, buffers and booking rules before the agent can use it. Retell AI lists appointment booking among the features a builder can add.

Goodcall's plan lists, as saved on 6 October 2026, do not mention calendar booking, so ask Goodcall before buying if booking is the main job. Whichever service you choose, make a test booking from start to finish before real callers use it.

items.q: Can I keep my business phone number with an AI receptionist?
items.a:
Yes, with Rosie, Goodcall, GoHighLevel's Voice AI and Retell AI alike, usually by forwarding calls. Rosie gives you a Rosie number and walks you through forwarding calls to it from your existing phone system whenever you want Rosie to answer, so the number customers already know stays the same. Goodcall assigns a number with an area code you pick and suggests conditional call forwarding, which passes calls over only when you don't answer or the line is busy.

GoHighLevel's Voice AI works only on LC Phone or Twilio numbers, so a business either ports its number into HighLevel or keeps it with its current carrier and forwards calls to a GoHighLevel number, which costs $1.15 a month for a local one. Retell AI charges $2.00 a month for its own numbers and nothing for numbers connected through your own telephony provider. Ask your current phone company whether it charges for forwarded calls before switching anything on.

items.q: Can an AI receptionist transfer a caller to a real person?
items.a:
Yes, but check the plan and the phone charges. Rosie offers warm transfers, where it briefs your team before connecting, and live transfers from its Scale plan up, and its Growth plan adds waterfall transfers that try several numbers until someone answers. Goodcall transfers calls to directory contacts: 3 on Starter, 25 on Growth and 500 on Scale. My AI Front Desk lists call transfer as an agent action, with 2 of each action type on its $99 plan. GoHighLevel's Voice AI has a Call Transfer action that sends the caller to a human phone number.

Metered platforms keep charging after the handover. Retell AI stops its AI fee once a call is transferred but keeps billing telephony, and HighLevel's Phone System guide bills both legs of a call forwarded to another US number, $0.02 a minute in all, though it does not say whether a Voice AI transfer counts as one.

items.q: Do AI receptionists charge for spam calls and hang-ups?
items.a:
It depends on what the service meters. Goodcall's pricing FAQ says robocalls, numbers you block and callers who never say anything to the agent do not count toward its allowance of unique callers, and a customer who calls 10 times in a month from the same number counts once. Rosie lists automatic spam detection on every plan, but its pricing page does not say whether screened calls use minutes.

Retell AI bills only calls that connect and, when a call reaches voicemail, only the time its agent is on the line; silence and hold time are billed because the agent keeps listening. GoHighLevel charges phone minutes for every call its number answers, each rounded up to a whole minute, plus Voice AI charges for the time its agent spends on the call, so a robocall the agent picks up is billed the same way as a real customer's call of the same length.

items.q: How long does it take to set up an AI receptionist?
items.a:
Ready-made services are the quickest to switch on. Rosie says it trains itself from your Google Business Profile and website, after which you confirm the details and add FAQs and message requirements, and it puts initial setup at as little as 10 minutes. My AI Front Desk advertises setup in 5 minutes. Those figures cover a first working version; calendar connections, transfer numbers and Zapier links to a CRM add steps.

GoHighLevel's Voice AI is assembled inside your account: create the agent, optionally from one of HighLevel's templates, adjust its prompt and welcome message, add actions such as booking or transfer, test it with a web or phone call, then deploy it to a number and set its hours, with a booking calendar configured beforehand. A custom agent on Retell AI usually takes the longest: Retell offers pre-built agent templates, but the integrations and call handling a receptionist needs are built and tested by whoever owns the project.

items.q: Does a GoHighLevel AI receptionist need A2P 10DLC registration?
items.a:
Almost certainly. HighLevel's A2P article calls A2P 10DLC the standard required to send texts to US mobile numbers from local business numbers, and says every business using its LC Phone system must register a brand and campaigns with The Campaign Registry. The article makes no exception for numbers that only take calls, and an agent that uses the Send SMS action, texts a booking confirmation or starts a workflow that sends a text needs registration in place before its first message.

Registration costs $22.50 once for a Sole Proprietor or Low Volume Standard brand, then a monthly campaign fee from $1.50, and both charges begin when the campaign is submitted, whether or not it is approved. After that, each text segment costs $0.00747 plus a carrier fee, on top of the call charges. Register before the agent goes live, so its first confirmation texts are not held up.
